narrative: Material PL1__M5AB9BBD shows erratic daily demand (CV=0.489) with no significant trend across the 143-day observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.717), with occasional spikes to 5 days against a mean of 1.60 days, making lead-time variance the dominant safety stock driver. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy was selected because demand is near-continuous (95.7% non-zero days) and the MOQ constraint makes periodic review less efficient. The order quantity is storage-capacity constrained at 5,423 units; the unconstrained EOQ of ~14,897 units would breach the 6,386-unit storage limit.
warnings: EOQ (14897 units) exceeds max_storage_units (6386.54); order_quantity capped to 5423 units by capacity constraint.
Inventory will peak at approximately 100% of available storage after each replenishment — monitor warehouse utilization closely.
Lead time CV=0.717 is high (unstable); safety stock is primarily driven by lead-time variability.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (95.7% non-zero fraction) with erratic amplitude, making a continuous-review reorder-point model more responsive than periodic review. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs; the hard MOQ of 1,683 is non-binding since EOQ >> MOQ.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity cap reduces the order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of ~14,897 to 5,423 units, increasing order frequency from ~8 to ~21 orders per year. This raises annual ordering cost but remains the cost-optimal feasible solution within the capacity envelope.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1,683) + safety_stock (963) = 2,646 units, which is within max_storage_units (6,386.54). No infeasibility conflict.
